messages:
maria_support: Hey — picking this up. Thanks for filing the escalation, @acme-secops. You said apt updates, pip installs, and docker pulls are failing from your Private deployment; could you paste the exact error you see?
acme-secops: Sure — here's a curl from one of the nodes hitting pypi:

acme-secops: ```
$ curl -v https://pypi.org/simple/
*   Trying 151.101.0.223:443...
* Connected to pypi.org (151.101.0.223) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* server certificate verification failed. CAfile: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt CRLfile: none
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) server certificate verification failed. CAfile: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt CRLfile: none
```

acme-secops: Docker pulls show a slightly different error:
acme-secops: ```
Error response from daemon: Get 'https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/': net/http: TLS handshake timeout
```

sam_se: Thanks. Two quick possibilities we've seen: 1) corporate TLS interception / proxy returning a cert signed by a private CA (apt/pip/dockerd all fail if that CA isn't trusted on the node), 2) SNI-based blocking where the firewall allows IP but drops TLS when SNI doesn't match.

maria_support: Can you run an openssl check from one of the failing nodes and paste output?
acme-secops: ```
$ openssl s_client -connect pypi.org:443 -servername pypi.org -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
...
depth=1 C = EU, ST = Example, O = Example Corp CA
verify error:num=19:self signed certificate in certificate chain
``` 

maria_support: Yep — that's a private CA in the chain. Two remediation paths:
- If the org is doing TLS interception, add their root CA to the nodes' system trust store (and to the Docker daemon trust store).
- Or bypass interception for our domains (recommended for production/public model pulls).

hugo_infra: To unblock quickly, here are the concrete egress entries we recommend allowing through the firewall (ports: 443 outbound). Please allow both hostname/DNS and these IP ranges where possible — many CDNs use large, changing ranges so DNS allowlisting is preferable.

hugo_infra: ```
Required hostnames (egress TCP/443):
- pypi.org
- files.pythonhosted.org
- pypi.io
- registry-1.docker.io
- auth.redwood.ai
- telemetry.redwood.ai
- model-registry.redwood.ai
- ghcr.io
- api.github.com
- raw.githubusercontent.com
- deb.debian.org
- security.ubuntu.com
- packages.debian.org
- storage.googleapis.com
- s3.amazonaws.com

Suggested IP prefixes (CDNs / docker registry fronts):
- 151.101.0.0/16 (Fastly / pypi)
- 3.224.0.0/12 (AWS ranges used by registries/CDNs)  # example — use provider published ranges
- 34.192.0.0/12

Ports: 443 outbound (HTTPS)
Note: registry-1.docker.io also uses other CDN frontends; prefer DNS allowlist.
```

sam_se: Also: if you must keep TLS interception, add the intercept CA to:
- /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ && run `update-ca-certificates` (Debian/Ubuntu)
- Docker: add CA to /etc/docker/certs.d/ or configure dockerd --insecure-registry carefully (we don't recommend insecure registry for public registries)

maria_support: For apt specifically, ensure Acquire::https::Verify-Peer 'true'; isn't being forced to false in apt config. If apt is failing with certificate errors, adding the CA to system trust fixes it.

acme-secops: We can add the CA but our security team is resistant to adding intercept CAs for external services. Can you provide a minimal list we can ask the firewall team to allow by SNI/DNS? They'll only whitelist by hostname.

hugo_infra: Understood. Minimal hostname list for Redwood functionality + package installs (DNS/SNI allowlist):
- auth.redwood.ai
- telemetry.redwood.ai
- model-registry.redwood.ai
- pypi.org
- files.pythonhosted.org
- registry-1.docker.io
- api.github.com
- raw.githubusercontent.com

maria_support: Quick repro steps we use to validate from your node once rules are in place:
1) curl -I https://auth.redwood.ai
2) curl -v https://pypi.org/simple/ | grep 'HTTP/'
3) docker pull hello-world
4) openssl s_client -servername pypi.org -connect pypi.org:443 | grep 'verify'

If any of those still show a private CA or TLS verify errors, capture `openssl s_client -showcerts` output and share.

acme-secops: Firewall team allowed the SNI hostnames above and we still see docker TLS timeouts for a subset of nodes.

sam_se: Two more checks:
- Do the nodes have DNS that returns public CDN IPs? `dig registry-1.docker.io` on the node.
- Is there any transparent proxy that rewrites SNI? `openssl s_client -servername registry-1.docker.io -connect registry-1.docker.io:443 -msg` should show the servername in the ClientHello.

acme-secops: dig returns an AWS CDN IP. openssl s_client shows the same intercept CA again on the failing node. On a working node (different subnet) it shows public cert from DigiCert.

hugo_infra: That means the failing subnet still passes traffic through the interception layer. Two options:
- Add the SNI exceptions at the intercepting proxy to bypass TLS interception for the hostnames above.
- Or centrally add the intercept CA to the system/Docker trust stores for nodes in that subnet (less ideal for compliance).

maria_support: One final note on model pulls: our model-registry may redirect through S3 URLs when downloading model artifacts. Make sure the firewall allows storage.googleapis.com and s3.amazonaws.com for large model downloads.

maria_support: I'll open a short internal ticket to flag common intercept-ca failures in our Private deployment docs (steps to check cert chain, minimal allowlist). In the meantime, letting us know whether the firewall team can add SNI bypass rules for the hostnames above or whether they want us to provide package-by-package IPs.

acme-secops: Firewall team will add SNI bypass for the listed hostnames. We'll re-run your repro steps and post results here shortly. Thanks everyone :pray: 

maria_support: Great — ping us with the openssl output if anything still looks wrong, and we can escalate to engineering if we see unexpected redirects or IPs that need permits.

install-bot: Deployment check completed for nodes in subnet-3: FAILED on cert verification (see above).

maria_support: Received. I'll follow up with a short checklist and the allowlist snippet you can hand to the firewall team.

maria_support: ```
Allowlist (SNI/DNS, outbound TCP 443):
- auth.redwood.ai
- telemetry.redwood.ai
- model-registry.redwood.ai
- pypi.org
- files.pythonhosted.org
- registry-1.docker.io
- ghcr.io
- api.github.com
- raw.githubusercontent.com
- storage.googleapis.com
- s3.amazonaws.com

Post-change tests:
- openssl s_client -servername pypi.org -connect pypi.org:443 -showcerts
- curl -I https://auth.redwood.ai
- docker pull hello-world
```

maria_support: Looping back after firewall change will help us close the ticket.
